title: Review of membrane_evo L7[L3]: up-vs-twin sweep on 2 of 3 viable new seeds, reversed on the third, from only 2-4 mutation flips per run under ~330 imposed disk deaths
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I looked at the pack (sheet, lineage, radial) and re-ran membrane_evo_up and its identical-event twin membrane_evo unchanged on new seeds 31-34 to T=40000 (share.py: K2 biomass share, cell counts and the event log; data/*.json), plus a labkit pack of the up arm on seed 32 (rerun/seed32). Seed 31: the population dies out in both arms by t~12000 (0 flips). Seed 32: up K2 share 0.15 (t=24k) -> 0.91 (t=40k), 14/17 cells K2-majority, vs twin 0.11. Seed 33: up 0.42 -> 0.94 (22/23 cells), twin 0.25. Seed 34: K2 arises late in up (0.26 at t=32k) and is lost (0.00 at 40k), twin 0.10. Each run has only 2-4 whole-cell flips (all the variation there is) against 313-344 imposed death-disk events. labkit on up seed 32: 6 persistent splits, max generation 3, L rim/core 1.40 (43/74 cells membrane-like).

observations.H: data/up_32.json vs data/tw_32.json: K2 share 0.91 vs 0.11; data/up_33.json vs tw_33.json 0.94 vs 0.25; data/up_34.json 0.00 vs tw_34 0.10 (reversed)

seeds_run.result: fail: K2 lost in up (0.00) vs twin 0.10

controls_run.H: identical-event twin membrane_evo on the same seeds: data/tw_31-34.json

verdicts.limitation: Sweep on 2/3 viable seeds (and 1/4 runs went extinct), so selection is real but not reliable. Variation is 2-4 whole-cell flips per run, so each sweep descends from one or two mutation origins; with ~330 imposed r=14 disk deaths per run, birth/death turnover is driven by the external disturbance, as the claim's own caveat says. I did not check conversions per mutation event, merge-aware births or off-kind daughters. The L ring is 1.40 aggregate (<1.5), so I list B as not checked rather than supported.
